positioning: A furniture-quality arcade for a real home: full-size controls, a coherent room and a guest experience that does not need a technician. The two-station custom concept is one acquisition option, not a promise that every factory game fits inside it.
audience: Primary: Mike, deciding per game whether to buy a factory cabinet, build it, or pursue a lawful donor system, and whether the two-station furniture concept is worth prototyping. Secondary, evaluated below rather than deferred: whether a furniture-and-integration offer to other hobbyists is a real business once a prototype exists.
thesis: Build for the physical experience, not the assumption that DIY is always cheaper. Compare each exact game with licensed home alternatives, prove the difficult control paths, and release a commercial batch only after demand and contribution survive a paid pilot.
thirtySecondPitch: A tiny putt, a clean strike, a fast hunting round and a shared jungle adventure: four reasons to gather around two well-designed stations. Buy proven parts and screens; make the furniture and integration distinctive. Compare complete licensed products before committing to custom hardware. Prototype the personal room first; make the production business earn its launch.

selectedDirection.name: Add the Missing Product Layer, Decide Make/Buy Per Game
selectedDirection.rationale: Lead with the finished room and the game's physical ritual, then expose make/buy, cash and technical release gates. Preserve the original plan's sound distinctions while correcting its missing market comparison and weak experiential presentation.

directions.name: PLAN.md's Existing Direction, Presented as Engineering
directions.summary: Keep PLAN.md's technical plan exactly as written -- two modular stations, per-game risk differentiation, rights excluded, no silent substitutions -- and present it the same way it already exists: numbered sections, dimensioned CAD drawings, a cost table with no competitive comparison.
directions.strength: Useful technical foundation: two control families, release-specific risk, rights boundaries and measurable acceptance.
directions.weakness: As a presentation it has no finished-product imagery, no stated buyer or promise, and never checked whether a licensed alternative already exists for any of the four games -- which is what actually reads as 'shallow and visually poor,' not the engineering itself.
directions.verdict: Rejected as the presentation direction. Carry forward the sound requirements, update the acquisition branches and strengthen the experience specification.

directions.name: Add the Missing Product Layer, Decide Make/Buy Per Game
directions.summary: Show the finished room and gameplay rituals first. Support them with per-game acquisition options, a bounded product offer and a reproducible production model.
directions.strength: Makes the product desirable without confusing design intent, listed products and measured compatibility.
directions.weakness: More moving parts than a single clean recommendation; still requires Mike to make per-game calls rather than receiving one finished answer.

directions.name: Documentary / Maker-Content Build
directions.summary: Frame the project as a personal hobby build, optionally documented for a blog or YouTube audience; not a product or business pitch.
directions.strength: Simple and honest; substantially lower commercial risk and liability exposure than running a product business; the content has independent value on its own.
directions.weakness: Discards the production/business evaluation Mike's mandate explicitly asked for; using this as the only direction would silently narrow scope he didn't approve.
directions.verdict: Rejected as the sole direction; its honesty about not assuming an audience carries into Direction B.

directions.name: Boutique Furniture / Integration Shop
directions.summary: Sell a defined furniture/control kit or separately quoted integration service. The initial offer excludes game software; customer-owned donor equipment requires an exact compatibility and rights review.
directions.strength: Separates the repeatable hardware offer from unpriced software-distribution rights and variable donor sourcing.
directions.weakness: Custom arcade suppliers already compete for this buyer. Price, room fit, serviceability and finish must justify a premium; no customer demand or differentiated performance is proven.
directions.verdict: Evaluated, not launched. See the business-case section for the actual reasoning and recommendation.

directions.name: Licensed Reseller / Installer
directions.summary: Become an authorized Incredible Technologies or Raw Thrills dealer, selling factory units plus custom furniture surrounds and installation.
directions.strength: An authorized relationship could supply a supported complete product rather than require self-sourced game media.
directions.weakness: Dealer eligibility, margin, minimum orders, warranty responsibility and permitted modifications are unknown. Licensing does not eliminate installation or product-liability obligations.
directions.verdict: Evaluate only after fresh authorization for specific vendor outreach. No relationship or terms are assumed.

chapters.headline: AFTER HOURS: two stations, four games
chapters.point: Open on a finished-product concept and room context, not an engineering drawing. Label the proposed two-station arrangement as a custom option whose final layout depends on exact game acquisition choices.
chapters.evidenceNeeded: ProductVisuals hero.png and room.png finished-product renders, labelled as concept renders.

chapters.headline: Buy or build? Check before you commit
chapters.point: Golden Tee Fore! Remastered ($2,499 pre-order) and Silver Strike Bowling: League Night ($4,699+) are real, factory-sold cabinets as of 2026-11-01, confirmed directly on Incredible Technologies' own store. Big Buck Hunter has a licensed cabinet too (Arcade1Up's Big Buck World), but it's a different game generation than the legacy Eagle-era titles PLAN.md's own research bench-recommended, and the exact generation Mike wants is still an open G0 choice. None of the three integrates into the brief's custom 760x610x950mm trackball furniture -- each is its own branded cabinet. This is a per-game decision, not a resolved recommendation.
chapters.evidenceNeeded: Competitor price table below, sourced to store.itsgames.com and arcade1up.com, observed 2026-11-01; ArcadeAdvisor's experience.json documenting both paths.
chapters.visual: Configuration-aware comparison table; no duplicate price chart.

chapters.headline: Mounted guns set the engineering bar
chapters.point: The inspected Raw Thrills 2015 documentation establishes mounted positional guns, original I/O and a security dongle. No open-source runtime or consumer-sized authorized substitute was established in this research. That is a bounded finding, not proof that no alternative exists for any Jurassic title. Preserve a complete legitimate donor path and a separate control prototype.
chapters.evidenceNeeded: ArcadeAdvisor's experience.json fidelityRisks and prototypeTest fields for Jurassic Park; research/game-feasibility.md and research/hardware-and-fabrication.md Jurassic branch sections.

chapters.headline: What you get. What you don't.
chapters.point: Four named targets remain in scope, but none is represented as running. No unauthorized game media, copied branding, authentication bypass or unproven compatibility is included. A factory cabinet is a room-layout alternative, not automatically a module inside the custom furniture.
chapters.evidenceNeeded: Product promise and exclusions text below; cross-reference BRIEF.md evidence boundary.

chapters.headline: What these prices actually prove
chapters.point: Listed Fore! Remastered plus League Night base prices sum to $7,198 before the required League Night TV, freight and tax. The custom two-station infrastructure allowance is $2,309-$4,377 before legitimate media/donors, mounted guns, labor, freight and tax. These are unlike scopes, so neither establishes a cheaper four-game delivered result. The production model separately prices one hardware kit, not the entire personal room.
chapters.evidenceNeeded: Observed configuration-aware listings; research/hardware-and-fabrication.md personal BOM; economics.json hardware-kit production assumptions.

chapters.headline: Is there a business here?
chapters.point: Evaluated, not deferred: the game-agnostic furniture/integration niche already has commercial players (VPCabs and comparable reproduction-cabinet builders). A new entrant needs a specific differentiator -- design process, materials, Mike's aesthetic -- not category novelty, and has zero demand evidence yet. The justified call right now is to prototype personally and run the validation plan below before committing to a launch, not to assume either a business exists or that it doesn't.
chapters.evidenceNeeded: Direction D definition above; ProductionAdvisor's economics.json SKU/scope section.

chapters.headline: What to decide before spending real money
chapters.point: Select exact games and a budget; prove the chosen control/runtime paths before fabrication. Commercial release additionally requires a defined SKU, paid pilot evidence, acceptable stressed contribution, funded cash needs and an independent safety/compliance review.
chapters.evidenceNeeded: Objections and validationPlan sections below; PLAN.md section 7 acceptance gates and section 8 decision ownership.

objections.objection: Why build when licensed factory products are listed?
objections.response: Buying may be the better answer for a selected game. Compare its exact release, stock, landed cost, controls and room footprint; do not preserve the custom concept merely because it has already been drawn.

objections.objection: Doesn't Arcade1Up's Big Buck World cabinet just solve Big Buck Hunter the same way Golden Tee Fore! solves golf?
objections.response: It may satisfy the request if its included Pro/World-era games are the desired ones. It does not reproduce the separate Eagle-era builds. Select the title rather than privileging the branch researched first.

objections.objection: Does buying a factory cabinet eliminate all legal or commercial risk?
objections.response: It removes the self-sourced ROM/media question for that game. It does not remove every risk: Silver Strike's Home Edition is confirmed, directly on the manufacturer's own page, as 'designed exclusively for home and non-commercial use' with Prize Play excluded, and it requires an ongoing paid subscription after Spring 2027 to keep online features. Read the actual terms of sale for Golden Tee Fore!, where the equivalent claim came from a reseller, not a confirmed manufacturer statement.

objections.objection: Are these factory alternatives actually purchasable right now?
objections.response: Not guaranteed, and evidence quality differs by product. Arcade1Up's own homepage directly confirms its Golden Tee 3D Deluxe cabinet is sold out. The Big Buck World cabinet's 'sold out' status comes only from a cached search-index snippet; a direct current read of that product URL redirects to Arcade1Up's homepage, so live stock is unresolved. Golden Tee Fore! Remastered's own page shows two different ship-date estimates. Reconfirm immediately before any purchase decision.

objections.objection: Does the cost case assume all four games come free once the furniture is built?
objections.response: No -- PLAN.md's own 'Separate unknowns and optional costs' section already says the infrastructure subtotal isn't the delivered price for all four games. This review repeats that and does not claim buying is cheaper than building either; no budget ceiling has been supplied.

objections.objection: Who would actually pay for a commercial version of this?
objections.response: Nobody validated yet, and the niche already has commercial players (VPCabs and comparable builders). The validationPlan below defines real tests -- including structured outreach, not just waiting for organic interest -- before treating this as more than a hypothesis.

objections.objection: The real Jurassic Park Arcade cabinet is $17,495+ and 1,217 lb -- is a basement build comparable?
objections.response: Not as a like-for-like attraction. The basement concept omits the environmental enclosure and motion and must separately prove its selected control/runtime path. The commercial cabinet remains a legitimate buy option where budget and access permit; a compact home counterpart was not established here.

validationPlan.hypothesis: The personal prototype can make the selected games enjoyable without recurring technical assistance.
validationPlan.test: Pass all four version-specific engineering acceptance gates, then observe five first-time guests using the documented controls and recovery flow. Proposed usability hurdle, not a measured result.
validationPlan.passSignal: All four game paths pass; at least four of five guests start and complete a chosen round without technical intervention after the brief onboarding.
validationPlan.failSignal: Any required game remains unproven, controls repeatedly miss inputs, or fewer than four guests complete the flow independently. Revise before finishing furniture.
validationPlan.costOfTest: Within the separately approved prototype budget; participant time and hardware are not assumed free.

validationPlan.hypothesis: Home-arcade buyers value coherent room design and serviceable full-size controls enough to consider a premium hardware kit.
validationPlan.test: After fresh approval, interview 20 qualified home-arcade buyers using a neutral concept and an explicit software-excluded offer. Run alongside the technical prototype, not after funding a factory. Record current alternatives, budget and specific unmet needs.
validationPlan.passSignal: Proposed discovery hurdle: at least eight independently describe a relevant unmet need and at least five request an itemized quote. This is directional evidence, not market-size validation.
validationPlan.failSignal: Fewer than five quote requests, or interest depends on included commercial games at the hardware-only price. Reposition or stop the product case.
validationPlan.costOfTest: Planning allowance: 20-30 hours; incentives and outreach spend require a separately approved cap. No outreach has occurred.

validationPlan.hypothesis: A defined kit can convert interest into paid orders at a price that covers fulfillment, support and acquisition costs.
validationPlan.test: After a real demo and costed SKU, quote ten qualified prospects the same scope and price. Observe conversion for 30 days. Accept orders only after approved terms, refund obligations and delivery capacity are in place.
validationPlan.passSignal: Proposed pilot hurdle: at least three unrelated buyers place paid pilot orders at a price with positive stressed contribution. Pilot satisfaction and repeatable build hours must pass before a larger batch; three orders do not justify 50 units.
validationPlan.failSignal: Fewer than three orders, demand only below the cost floor, unresolved refunds, or pilot support erases margin. Do not release speculative inventory.
validationPlan.costOfTest: Use the production model for pilot cash, paid labor and reserves. Customer deposits remain liabilities until performance, not free funding.

validationPlan.hypothesis: Authorized resale or integration could be more attractive than manufacturing a kit.
validationPlan.test: With fresh approval for each vendor contact, request written dealer eligibility, wholesale margin, minimum orders, territory, modification limits and warranty responsibilities.
validationPlan.passSignal: Written terms plus a scope-matched landed-cost and support model meet the same cash and contribution gates as the custom offer.
validationPlan.failSignal: Unavailable authorization, insufficient margin, unacceptable minimum order or unsupported modifications. Keep the personal acquisition and commercial product decisions separate.
validationPlan.costOfTest: Research and negotiation time; no assumed agreement, application payment or vendor commitment.
